Childhood recitation and examination success at ages 7 and 11, without a calendar year.

work.en: In the chamber, be ashamed before the leaking roof

translationRepairs: At the beginning Dezong, having suffered many hardships, sought to indulge the frontier commands; whenever a commander died, he sent eunuchs to observe the army and see whom the masses wished to install — so great generals privately used gold and silks to court the inner court and seek a commission; in the late Yan years this was especially so, and regional picks did not come from the court.

At the beginning Dezong, having suffered many hardships, sought to indulge the frontier commands; whenever a commander died, he sent eunuchs to observe the army and see whom the masses wished to install — so great generals privately used gold and silks to court the inner court and seek a commission; in his late years this was especially so, and regional picks did not come from the court.
晏年 means Dezong's late years, not a Yan era; the original invents a period name.
He died the following year at seventy, was posthumously made Sikong, and given the temple name Xuanxian.
He died the following year at seventy, was posthumously made Situ, and given the posthumous title Xuanxian.
贈司徒 is a posthumous Situ, distinct from 司空 in the previous sentence, and 謚 is a posthumous title, not a temple name.
The next year he died, age seventy; posthumously made Sikong, posthumous title Xuanxian.
The next year he died, age seventy; posthumously made Situ, posthumous title Xuanxian.
The source grants 司徒, not 司空; Sikong is the honorary office already named in the preceding sentence.
After Xiao Ye's fall, eunuchs ruined him; Jiang Shen was chosen instead, Sheng was made honorary Minister of Rites and exiled to Tianping, where he died in frustration.
After Xiao Ye's fall, eunuchs ruined him; Jiang Shen was chosen instead, Sheng was made honorary Minister of Rites and sent out as military commissioner of Tianping, where he died in frustration.
出為天平節度使 is an outward posting as military commissioner, not exile.

When Ji and historiographer Jiang Wu submitted Dezong's Veritable Record, Jifu argued that Ji, having left the history office on grounds of illness, should not present it, and had him made Grand Mentor while dismissing the historians.

When Ji and historiographer Jiang Wu submitted Dezong's Veritable Record, Jifu argued that Ji, having left the history office on grounds of illness, should not present it, and had him made Advisor to the Heir Apparent while dismissing the historians.
太子賓客 is Advisor to the Heir Apparent, not Grand Mentor (the later 太子太傅). The proposed Chinese gloss is accurate but awkward in idiomatic English.
Past forty years, distressed between Guangyang, he did not rouse himself; wife and children pursued blame — Fan was at ease as before.
Past forty years, distressed in Guangling, he did not rouse himself; wife and children pursued blame — Fan was at ease as before.
廣陵 is Guangling; Guangyang is a wrong place-name, and 間 here is not “between.”

When Jianfeng died, Haozhou prefect Du Jian hastily drove to arrive, secretly having a downward look; Fan wept and said: "You, sir, now in mourning — you ought carefully to guard the soil; why abandon and come?

When Jianfeng died, Haozhou prefect Du Jian hastily drove to arrive, secretly having ambitious designs; Fan wept and said: "The lord now has died — you, sir, ought carefully to guard your territory; why abandon it and come?
公今喪 refers to Jianfeng's death; 君 is Du Jian, who is told to keep his own territory, while 陰有顗望 marks ambitious designs, not a downward look.
They performed vulgar Yuzhou skits. Fan excused himself once and said, "I spend the day with you yet cannot understand a word!"
They performed comic skits and riddling talk. Fan excused himself after one visit and said, "I spend the day with you yet cannot understand a word!"
庾語 is riddling, enigmatic speech, not the toponym Yuzhou; 俳說 is comic jesting.
Zhongshu and others made comic skits with Yuzhou dialect mutually intimate; Fan on seeing once, apologized and did not go, saying: "I with you all day — I do not understand what language is spoken!

Zhongshu and others made comic skits and riddling talk in familiar jest; Fan on seeing them once apologized and did not go, saying: "I spend the whole day with you and do not understand what is being said!"
庾語 is riddling talk, not a Yuzhou dialect; 相狎昵 is familiar jest, and Fan declined after one visit.
When Zheng Yin was dismissed, he was therefore appointed Vice Minister of the Secretariat and Associate Director.
When Zheng Yin was dismissed, he was therefore appointed Vice Minister of the Chancellery and Associate Manager of Affairs with the Secretariat-Chancellery.
門下侍郎 is a Chancellery vice-ministership, not a Secretariat post, but the proposed English embeds Chinese characters and must be given in English only.
When Congshi sent Wang Yiyuan to court, Ji won him with calm persuasion until Yiyuan described Congshi's crimes ripe for action; Ji had already secured the loyalty of generals such as Wu Chongyin.

When Congshi sent Wang Yiyuan to court, Ji won him with calm persuasion until Yiyuan described Congshi's crimes as ripe for action; Ji had recently sent people over and obtained the key cooperation of Congshi's great generals such as Wu Chongyin.
比遣往 is a recent dispatch, not a prior fait accompli, and 要領 is the essential hold on Congshi's generals, not loyalty already secured.
He died before taking post at fifty-eight, was posthumously made Vice Minister of Revenue, and given the temple name Zhenjian.
He died before taking post at fifty-eight, was posthumously made Minister of Revenue, and given the posthumous name Zhenjian.
戶部尚書 is Minister of Revenue, not vice minister, and 謚 is a posthumous name, not a temple name.
Before departing he died, age fifty-eight; posthumously made Vice Minister of Revenue, posthumous title Zhenjian.
Before departing he died, age fifty-eight; posthumously made Minister of Revenue, posthumous title Zhenjian.
尚書 is the ministerial rank; vice minister would be 侍郎.
He was the eighth-generation descendant of Northern Zhou pillar of state Wei.
He was the eighth-generation descendant of Northern Zhou pillar of state Xiong.
The ancestor named in the source is 敻 (Xiong); rendering that given name as Wei drops the name the text actually supplies.
Great-great-grandson eight generations removed of Zhou pillar of state Wei.
Eighth-generation descendant of the Later Zhou pillar of state Xiong.
八世孫 is an eighth-generation descendant, not a great-great-grandson, and the named ancestor is 敻 of the Later Zhou.
He was later made Vice Director of the Secretariat.
He was later made Vice Director of the Palace Library.
秘書少監 belongs to the Palace Library (秘書省), not the Secretariat.
After a long time, changed to Vice Director of the Secretariat.
After a long time, changed to Vice Director of the Palace Library.
秘書少監 is not a Secretariat office.
The next day Fan was demoted to Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
The next day Fan was demoted to Chief of the Household of the Heir Apparent.
太子詹事 is the heir's household administration, not Grand Mentor (太傅).
Su and others slandered him and, debating war before the emperor, had him demoted to Vice Minister of Personnel.
Su and others slandered him; he also debated military affairs with Du before the emperor, and the discussion went largely against him, so he was demoted to Vice Minister of Personnel.
The original omits 與度 as debate counterpart and compresses 議頗駁, which records that the discussion went against Guanzhi.
He was demoted to Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent at the eastern capital.
He was demoted to Supervisor of the Household of the Heir Apparent, assigned to the eastern capital.
太子詹事 is the heir's household supervisor, not Grand Mentor, and 分司東都 is an eastern-capital assignment.
Zhou Chi of Zheng-Hua took him onto staff.
Zhou Chi, military commissioner of Zheng-Hua, memorialized to place him on his staff.
節度鄭滑 names Zhou Chi's military commission, not his native place, and 表署幕府 is a memorialized staff appointment.
He died, was posthumously Vice Minister of Revenue, and styled Zhen.
He died, was posthumously made Minister of Revenue, and given the posthumous title Zhen.
戶部尚書 is Minister of Revenue, not vice minister, and 謚曰貞 is a posthumous title.
When Dengzhou prefect Xue Hongzong was dismissed, the emperor's admonition drawn from the book astonished every official.
When Dengzhou prefect Xue Hongzong attended the thanksgiving audience, the emperor's admonition on prefectural affairs astonished every official.
中謝 is the thanksgiving audience after appointment, not dismissal, and 敕戒州事 is an admonition on prefectural affairs.
In Taihe 5 the ancestral temple leaked; Wenzong, angry at delay, stripped officials and ordered eunuchs to repair.
In Taihe 5 the ancestral temple leaked; Wenzong, angry at delay, blamed Director Li Rui and Supervisor Wang Kan, stripped their salaries, and ordered eunuchs to repair.
The source names Director Li Rui and Supervisor Wang Kan and records that their salaries were stripped, which the original English omits.

At first, Wen concurrently served as lecturer-reader to Crown Prince Zhuangyi. In the morning he went to the palace; at midday he saw the Crown Prince and remonstrated: "Your Highness is in flourishing years. You should rise at cockcrow and ask after the Son of Heaven's well-being, following King Wen's precedent."

At first, Wen concurrently served as lecturer-reader to Crown Prince Zhuangke. In the morning he went to the palace; at midday he saw the Crown Prince and remonstrated: "Your Highness is in flourishing years. You should rise at cockcrow and ask after the Son of Heaven's well-being, following King Wen's precedent."
莊恪 is Zhuangke; 恪 is ke, not the yi of 懿.

Wang Yanping left Lingwu with horses and armor, bribed his way from Kangzhou registrar to Fuzhou marshal; musician Yuchi Zhang was made Guangzhou chief administrator — Wen sealed and returned all such edicts.

Wang Yanping left Lingwu with horses and armor, bribed his way from Kangzhou registrar to Fuzhou marshal; musician Yuchi Zhang was made Guang prefecture chief administrator — Wen sealed and returned all such edicts.
光州 is Guang Prefecture, not 廣州 (Guangzhou).
At the time many straightened his words.
At the time many regarded his words as upright.
直其言 means contemporaries judged the speech upright, not that they straightened the wording.

Yao Xu, an investigating official of the Salt and Iron Monopoly, handled major cases; the emperor considered him able and promoted him to Director of the Bureau of Appointments, Outer Section. As he was about to hurry to the ministry, Wen sent a household member to stop him and immediately memorialized: "The pure selection of gentlemen-officials cannot be used to reward capable clerks."

Yao Xu, an investigating official of the Salt and Iron Monopoly, handled major cases; the emperor considered him able and promoted him to Director of the Bureau of Operations, Outer Section. As he was about to hurry to the ministry, Wen sent a household member to stop him and immediately memorialized: "The pure selection of gentlemen-officials cannot be used to reward capable clerks."
職方員外郎 is the Bureau of Operations, not Appointments.
Female craft adept at literature — continued Lady Cao's Admonitions for Women — circulated in the world.
She was skilled at literature — continued Lady Cao's Admonitions for Women — circulated in the world.
女工屬文 takes the daughter as subject skilled at composing, not “female craft” as needlework.
